data.name: Title
data.value: Broad permissions on LAPS password attributes

data.name: EncryptedRead
data.value: This attribute stores an encrypted LAPS password. Read permission allows retrieval of the encrypted value, if present; it does not by itself grant permission to decrypt it. This finding does not establish that this principal can obtain the local administrator password or take control of the machine.

data.name: ClearTextRead
data.value: This attribute stores a LAPS password in clear text. If a password value is present, reading it exposes the local administrator password and may enable local administrative access.

data.name: EveryAttributeReach
data.value: The supporting entries reach every attribute on this object rather than only this LAPS attribute. Whether Control Access is also required follows the captured schema flags.

data.name: WhyItMatters
data.value: Captured permissions and membership connect a broad principal to LAPS password attributes. Established read permission may expose a clear-text password if one is stored; encrypted values need separate decryption permission. Conditional entries or incomplete evidence do not establish read access. This is named-holder permission evidence and captured membership attribution, not an individual user's authorization, password retrieval or machine takeover.

data.name: WhatToDo
data.value: Review all recorded grants and membership routes before changing an intended delegation. Removing one displayed grant or membership route may not remove every way to read these attributes. If access is unintended, narrow the permission or remove the broad membership while retaining access needed by your administrators. The originating container was not captured; verify the actual source before changing an inherited delegation. Read permission does not establish permission to decrypt encrypted values.

data.name: About
data.value:
Reports captured broad read-permission exposures for the three current LAPS password attributes on computer objects, including disabled accounts.
Read Property is required. Control Access is additionally required when the captured schema establishes confidentiality. Unknown schema, unsupported scope, conditional entries, incomplete permissions and membership limitations remain explicit. Known supporting exposures are retained without implying complete access analysis.
One finding is retained per computer and broad identity, preserving independent holder/attribute exposures rather than only one representative grant. A captured membership path is a witness, not an enumeration of every possible route.
An inherited-class scope marker is not an originating container. Disabling an AD computer account does not remove stored directory material or establish the state of a local account.
This rule collects no password values and establishes neither individual-user authorization, password presence, decryption nor a completed path to Tier 0.
